name: "Provided to YouTube by <distributor>" Art Track description block
type: Metadata parsing — identifier via regex-parseable, label/distributor-supplied plain-text description block
maintainer: Distributor/label-supplied content, delivered through Google's 'Art Track' auto-generated-video product for audio releases without a dedicated video asset; Google operates the ingestion pipeline, but the actual text is authored/templated by rights-holders and aggregators (DistroKid, CD Baby, TuneCore, The Orchard, major-label distribution arms, etc.) at release time, not by Google or the end uploader.
required_input: Video description text only — sourced from Data API videos.list snippet.description, Innertube /player's videoDetails.shortDescription, or watch-page HTML. No audio needed.
classification_or_hitrate: When the marker text is present, field-extraction precision is high because the block is a fixed, distributor-templated format authored by the rights-holder rather than free text from an arbitrary uploader. Recall is limited to genuine 'Art Track' uploads specifically — auto-generated videos created for audio-only releases lacking a dedicated video asset — a meaningful but partial slice of all Content-ID-covered music, distinct from official music videos, live-session uploads, or user reuploads, none of which carry this text. The exact template has minor documented variants across distributors and eras (older uploads sometimes omit the ℗ line or the 'Released on' line; some use different separator punctuation between track and artist), so a single rigid regex can under-match a nontrivial minority of otherwise-valid blocks. [uncertain]
pitch_speed_cover_robustness: Same structural limitation as the Topic-channel and engagement-panel signals: this is per-video upload metadata tied to one canonical Art Track upload, not derived from audio analysis, so it provides zero coverage for sped-up/nightcore/pitch-shifted reuploads or cover versions, which by definition would not be genuine label-issued Art Track uploads carrying this exact text.
catalog_language_bias: Skews toward the same aggregator-distributed catalog as the Topic-channel signal (music routed through DistroKid/CD Baby/TuneCore/The Orchard and similar, covering a broad multi-language range including substantial K-pop/J-pop content when routed digitally) but excludes any music never packaged as an Art Track — visual-first official music videos, live sessions, and anime OSTs uploaded directly by a label's branded channel using a custom, non-templated description format fall outside this signal. [uncertain]
evaluation_dataset: None official/benchmarked; the format and a working regex for it are documented informally through developer-community discussion (Stack Overflow-style threads and issue trackers such as ytdl-org/youtube-dl#26013 and yt-dlp#622/#3847/#8971), not a formal labeled evaluation set.
confidence_calibration: No numeric score is emitted, but a successful match against the strict 'Provided to YouTube by' anchor text can reasonably be treated as a high, fixed-confidence result given the text is label/distributor-authored and not editable by the uploader, unlike free-text titles.
api_availability: Free — the description text is obtained through whichever transport is already in use (the free-tier-quota Data API, or free HTML/Innertube scraping); no separate paid service exists specifically for this signal.
chrome_extension_usability: Pure client-side regex execution over text already available from another call; no additional network request and no incremental CORS/host_permissions requirement beyond whatever already-fetched description text is being reused.
client_vs_server: Entirely local regex parsing; no data beyond the already-retrieved description text is sent anywhere.
bundle_weight_cold_start: Negligible — a compiled regular expression run once per description, effectively sub-millisecond marginal cost.
breakage_risk: Moderate — the free-text description is distributor-controlled rather than a single Google-maintained schema, and has shown minor field-order/label variants historically (presence/absence of a 'Released on' line, presence/absence of explicit 'Writer(s):'/'Composer(s):' lines, differing track/artist separator characters), so a hardcoded regex needs periodic tuning against real-world samples across distributors and eras. That said, the overall template has remained recognizable for years since it is a fixed auto-generation product rather than a live-rendered UI surface, making it comparatively more stable than the unversioned renderer JSON that Items 2/3 depend on. [uncertain]
realtime_capability: Yes, effectively instant once the description text is already in hand from another call.
identification_fields: track/song title, artist, album, release year and/or release date, and often the distributor/label name — no ISRC is printed in the visible description text itself, though the underlying label/distributor pipeline that generated the block does hold an ISRC internally that is simply not surfaced here. [uncertain] Generally more reliable than generic title/channel-string heuristics precisely because the block is rights-holder-authored rather than uploader-authored.
isrc_availability: No — not present in the visible description text (present only in the distributor's internal metadata, not exposed by this signal). [uncertain]
tos_restrictions: Same general ToS caveat as Items 2/3 applies only if the description text is sourced via free HTML/Innertube scraping (automated-access clause); if instead sourced via the official Data API's videos.list description field, this specific data point is fully ToS-compliant regardless of what regex is subsequently applied to already-authorized API output.
risk_tolerance_note: Lower incremental risk than Items 2/3/4 in isolation, since the underlying description text is commonly retrievable via the fully official Data API path — the 'unofficial' risk profile only attaches if it is instead sourced via free HTML/Innertube scraping rather than the keyed API.
cascade_position: Enrichment — runs after an initial music/non-music gate (e.g. the Topic-channel check or engagement-panel presence) to extract a more structured, higher-confidence title/artist/album/release-date than generic title-string heuristics, and is particularly valuable as a fallback specifically when the 'Music in this video' panel (Items 2/3) is absent but the upload is nonetheless a genuine Art Track.
failure_mode: Fails silently — a non-match simply yields no structured result and the pipeline falls through to weaker title-heuristic parsing; low risk of a confidently-wrong answer overall because the anchor text 'Provided to YouTube by' is distinctive and very unlikely to false-positive-match a genuinely non-music description.
cost_model_at_scale: $0 — regex execution over already-available text, no incremental cost regardless of volume.
geo_region_availability: Subject to the same territory-scoped Content-ID/licensing gating as Items 2/3/4 for whether the Art Track exists or is visible in a given region at all; once visible, the description text itself carries no further region restriction.
